claim_limits: Shipping mode C: radar comparison not completed; only terrain distances are reported (PRD 4).

Earth windows: every 5 km UTM square of the holuhraun search region (G0-04) whose corners lie inside the region polygon; eligibility from the T3 valid fraction and the config WorldCover rule at the nearest class of each 90 m cell centre.
Both windows are resampled on a sphere (D29 aeqd_sphere); on Earth this approximates the WGS84 ellipsoid over a 5 km window.
The nu values use the direction_mean isotropic summary of T3.
Copernicus GLO-30 is a surface model (DSM) of one epoch; snow, moisture and surface change since acquisition were not checked on the Earth window.
This is a slice search over the configured regions, not the full t5 search; the shortlist is the first Pareto layer of the windows compared.
PGDA78 error spatial correlation is not propagated: the uncertainty components (clones, scenarios) have not been run.
PGDA78 Site01 interpolation: 0.1045 of the target window's valid 90 m cells sit on a 5 m pixel with at least one LOLA return; the rest of the 5 m DEM there is interpolated.

WorldCover 2021 at the Earth window's 90 m cell centres: allowed classes 1.0000, of which snow_ice 0.0000 (allowed by config earth_search.masks; PRD-04 reports snow and ice separately), permanent water 0.0000.
This Earth window is the G0-05 first-card window (the eligible window containing the decoded UAVSAR ROI centre), chosen at G0 without ranking by similarity.
Mode C: radar comparison not completed. The radar inputs were not qualified within the pilot, so no radar distance or radar signature is part of this card.
The encoder is EXPERIMENTAL (G5 NOT_RUN); its distance, if shown, is Predicted and takes no part in any ranking.
Field confirmation is future work; similarity here does not establish block sizes, soil strength, buried structure or low-gravity mobility (PRD 3).

limits: Gravity: about one-sixth of Earth's on the Moon.
Atmosphere: wind, rain, weathering and erosion shape Earth surfaces; none act on the Moon.
Water and life: Earth ground carries moisture and biology; lunar regolith is dry apart from possible polar volatiles.
Radiation and space weathering act directly on the lunar surface.
Temperature: permanently shadowed lunar ground is far colder than any Earth surface.
Illumination: the Sun stays near the horizon at the lunar pole.
Regolith origin: lunar soil is made by impacts, with sharp, unweathered grains unlike most Earth sediments.
